stem.text: A particle moves along the x-axis. Its position at time t seconds is \( x(t) = - 2 t^{3} + 3 t^{2} + 33 t \) meters, for \( t \ge 0 \). Find the speed of the particle at time t = 3, and determine whether the speed is increasing or decreasing at that time. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The speed is 3 meters per second, and it is increasing at that time, because \( v(3) = -3 \) and \( a(3) = -30 \) have the same sign.

worked_solution.text: Velocity is the derivative of position, \( v(t) = - 6 t^{2} + 6 t + 33 \), so \( v(3) = -3 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: velocity is the derivative of position

worked_solution.text: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, \( a(t) = 6 - 12 t \), so \( a(3) = -30 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: acceleration is the derivative of velocity

worked_solution.text: The speed is \( \left|v(3)\right| = 3 \) meters per second.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed is the absolute value of velocity

worked_solution.text: Because \( v(3) = -3 \) and \( a(3) = -30 \) have the same sign, the speed of the particle is increasing at t = 3.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed increases when velocity and acceleration share a sign

options.label: The speed is 72 meters per second, and it is decreasing at that time, because \( v(3) = 72 \) and \( a(3) = -3 \) have opposite signs.
options.derivation: the position read as the velocity and the velocity as the acceleration, one differentiation too few
